text:
Recent work supports rank-based diagnostics over raw score margins: sampled evaluation can change model ordering, and popularity sampling does not reliably reproduce full-catalog ranking. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study compares random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive negatives across three datasets with repeated runs, showing that sampler effects depend on dataset characteristics. Popularity-matched negatives therefore offer a useful stress test, but are not validated substitutes for full-catalog evaluation. [Sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [evaluation comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045).

Temporal generalization deserves a separate probe. *Time to Split* (2025) shows that leave-one-out evaluation can overlap training and evaluation periods and change model rankings. *SplitLight* (2026) audits temporal leakage, cold-start exposure and distribution shifts. For this task, a proposed diagnostic would reserve chronological suffixes within training data and fit diagnostic checkpoints only on preceding interactions, leaving benchmark splits unchanged. Training-derived popularity bins, history-length groups and timestamp cohorts can expose failures without unavailable reviews or simulator traits. [Time to Split](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16289), [SplitLight](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.19339).

Suggested experiment: on fixed training-only diagnostic users, compare uniform-99, popularity-matched-99 and chunked full-catalog ranks; report HR@10, target-rank percentiles, hit disagreement and checkpoint-order agreement. Across four categories, report individual HR@10 and paired user-bootstrap uncertainty for the equal-weight macro improvement; bootstrap intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed variability. Test whether diagnostics predict subsequent pinned validation gains rather than assuming validity. Keep pinned macro validation HR@10 as the selection objective; cap diagnostic users/checkpoints and record GPU seconds. These are proposed probes, not measured findings.
